# PAYG instalments
You may be required to make pay as you go (PAYG) instalments when you earn business and investment income.

# Calculate your PAYG instalments
## Use the instalment rate (option 2)
1. Enter your instalment income for the period (usually a quarter) at **T1** on your activity statement.
   - Generally, your [instalment income](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/payg-instalments/calculate-your-payg-instalments/instalment-income) is your gross business and investment income, excluding GST.

## If you think your payment amount is too high or too low
Instalment income is your gross business and investment income, excluding GST.

# Instalment income
## Income you do not include
- income such as salary and wages, where amounts were withheld or should have been withheld under the PAYG withholding system. However, if amounts were withheld because you did not provide your TFN or ABN, the income is included in instalment income

Instalment income is your gross business and investment income, excluding GST.

QC68096

# Who can pay using the instalment amount
## Who is eligible to pay using the instalment amount
- an individual (including sole traders)
- a super fund that
  - has business and investment income of $2 million or less
- a company that
  - has business and investment income of $2 million or less
  - is a [small business entity](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/incentives-and-concessions/small-business-cgt-concessions/small-business-cgt-concessions-eligibility-conditions/cgt-small-business-entity-eligibility) with an aggregated turnover of less than $10 million

web.description:
# To vary or not to vary? PAYG instalments for the new financial year
## What is a PAYG instalment?
The Pay As You Go (PAYG) instalment system requires certain taxpayers deriving business or investment income to pay instalments progressively towards their income tax liability.

## Who is required to pay PAYG instalments?
A taxpayer only needs to pay PAYG instalments if they have been notified by the ATO, typically through myGov, Online services for business or by mail.

for an individual (including a sole trader) or trust, they have:

- Business and investment income in their most recent tax return of $4,000 or more

- Have business and investment income in their most recent tax return of $2 million or more

## How many PAYG instalments are payable?
Taxpayers with business and investment income of more than $20 million are required to make monthly PAYG instalments.

## PAYG instalment payment options
Companies with business and investment income over $2 million that are not small or medium business entities (aggregated turnover less than $50 million) are not eligible to pay using the predetermined instalment amount.
